feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good scope and relevance: combines strategy, web/CMS, analytics, multimedia, and governance in a way that fits modern digital leadership roles.  
- Generally strong writing: concise, professional, and easy to follow, with solid examples such as the 10,000+ page migration and in-house studio build.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (engagement growth, efficiency gains, revenue/supporter impact, adoption rates).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; use consistent serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—prefer “French: A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper leadership/value angle would improve impact.

- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your seniority and strongest differentiators: enterprise digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a more concise formulation such as “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, editorial workflow design, stakeholder coordination, and translating complex policy or technical issues into clear, audience-focused content. Strong background in advocacy messaging, platform governance, and building scalable systems that improve execution across web, email, social, and multimedia channels.”

- “Stakeholder coordination,” “workflow/systems,” and “advocacy messaging” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Web, email, social, and multimedia” is repeated extensively throughout Work Experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, senior-level terms: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication”; “Web platform governance & CMS administration” instead of “Web & CMS administration.”
- Group related items to reduce list fatigue and improve parallel structure; suggested version: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Systems architecture & process improvement • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Keep style consistent: use plural “communications” and parallel noun phrases throughout.
- Consider trimming to 7–8 items if space is tight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, advocacy messaging, analytics, and multimedia.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also duplicates Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around distinctive consulting impact, named platforms, and 2–3 measurable outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets and lead with outcomes: combine digital systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on what improved (speed, consistency, reporting, publishing quality, stakeholder alignment).
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more concrete: mention Drupal, microsites, modular content architecture, toolkits, front-end implementation, and troubleshooting in one concise bullet.
- Add metrics wherever possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaigns launched, reduction in publishing time, engagement lift, search success, or adoption of the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, enterprise web improvement” repeats language already used in the summary and NACo Director role.
- AI-enabled search is also featured in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and reserve technical detail for the project section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. Tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation work, and add outcome language so it reads less like a scope summary and more like a results-driven director role.

Suggested edit
- Replace the first sentence with a sharper headline: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website transformation and outcome: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel ownership more strategic and measurable: include email/social performance if available (growth, engagement, CTR, list size, campaign results), not just audience size.
- Strengthen impact phrasing: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy, events, and recurring multimedia programming”; “Expanded analytics stack… to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Email/newsletters, video programming, and workflow improvements overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.
- “Governance/publishing standards/planning systems” may duplicate summary/skills language unless tied to a concrete operational result.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item reads generic and overlaps with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned before stepping into broader leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + ownership: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show channel-building impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine planning/workflow bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed” or “oversaw execution” here.
- Weekly video/livestream language also appears in the prior role; frame this item as scaling and operationalizing the program, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctiveness rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording tied to current work: “Enterprise web and content strategy,” “Editorial governance and publishing operations,” “Cross-channel communications systems leadership.”
- Swap “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for a more differentiated capability such as “Mission-driven stakeholder communications” or “Public-sector digital communications strategy.”
- Make “Audience-focused content planning” more senior and operational: “Audience strategy and content architecture” or “Audience-centered content operations.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Enterprise web and content strategy • Editorial governance and publishing operations • Cross-channel communications systems leadership • Public-sector digital communications strategy • Audience strategy and content architecture”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo role bullets; keep this section higher-level and less repetitive.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills block, make it more strategic, grouped, and aligned to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capabilities, not a flat list: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Replace “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with “front-end implementation” unless hands-on coding depth is essential for the target role.
- Put the most relevant/recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations.
- If space allows, sharpen one phrase to outcomes-oriented language: “CMS modernization for large public-facing sites” or “AI-enabled search for complex content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave detailed tools there.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory. Tighten it to emphasize strategic analytics capability and avoid repeating the near-identical “Technical + IT” section.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Decision-ready reporting” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure for 10,000+ pages / 3.5M annual page views.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools here; move lower-signal items to Technical + IT if needed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- “SEO and performance analysis” may also partially duplicate broader optimization language elsewhere; keep wording distinct.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value production leadership and delivery capabilities most relevant to recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production” instead of “Video production and editing.”
- Group skills by delivery scope, e.g.: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio operations • Virtual event production”
- Consider adding a leadership/operational angle tied to recent experience: “In-house studio production” or “Recurring advocacy programming”
- Keep tool-level detail out of this section; leave software specifics to “Multimedia & Creative Tools.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; use distinct phrasing or remove one.
- “PTZ camera systems” is quite narrow for a topline section unless supported elsewhere; it may fit better under Technical + IT.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use it to signal depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than repeat a flat tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** only works if Drupal-led work is the focus; consider adding qualifiers.
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add level cues instead of more platforms: **Drupal (advanced)**, **WordPress/SharePoint (working knowledge)**, etc.
- Use consistent naming: change **Power Pages** to **Microsoft Power Pages** for clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2]; consider trimming one list or making this version more implementation-specific.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere; remove if it’s not relevant to target roles.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **JavaScript • HTML5/CSS3 • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • jQuery**
- Consider adding light proficiency framing if accurate: **JavaScript, HTML5/CSS3 (implementation); API integrations; GTM; Cloudflare Workers; GitHub Actions; legacy jQuery**
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented via parenthetical context: **API integrations (workflow/data connections) • GTM (tracking deployment) • GitHub Actions (deployment automation)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already appear in **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one version shorter or remove repeated terms there.
- **GitHub Actions** may also overlap conceptually with **Automation & Workflow Systems**; keep it here only if you want this section to signal developer tooling.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing systems-building over chat/collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Project Systems**
- Reorder by relevance to recent work: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello**
- Move lower-signal collaboration tools out unless required by the role: **Slack • Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light functional framing instead of a flat list: **Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project operations: Jira, Asana, Trello**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams also risk reading as basic workplace tools rather than differentiating technical capability.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the strategic/operational value of email systems. It should signal enterprise email, member communications, and journey/campaign execution rather than read as a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- If keeping as a skills line, tighten to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add scope/value: **Enterprise email marketing, member communications and automated journey platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- Put **Higher Logic** first if it was the primary platform at NACo; order tools by most recent/highest-credibility use, not alphabetically.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work-experience bullets already covering email/newsletters; avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here.
- “Engagement” is broad; don’t imply CRM ownership unless that responsibility is evidenced elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles on workflows, video, and digital operations. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete scope or outputs if available.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as early-career build phase: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Emphasize distinct contributions: website refresh support, livestream/event production, weekly video production, and junior staff guidance.
- Add measurable detail where possible: number of livestreams/events, cadence of weekly videos, audience reach, or size/scope of the website refresh.
- Tighten wording: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, support a major website refresh, produce livestreams and weekly video updates, and guide a digital media associate across daily publishing operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia” repeats language used in later NACo roles; keep this entry more tactical.
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as production/launch rather than program leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize project coordination plus one standout, first-of-its-kind achievement.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace generic phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer scope and purpose.
- If possible, add outputs or scale: number of projects, episodes, stakeholders, or programs supported.
- Suggested rewrite: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams, helping translate county-focused research into digital and multimedia content. Launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production coordination and rollout.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and research/program support.
- Avoid overemphasizing video or channel management here, since those are stronger and more recent in later roles.
